about.title: About BuyTime
about.a1: BuyTime is a Hong Kong mall parking receipt trading platform. You can sell unused parking validation receipts, or buy receipts from other users at a discount to save on parking fees.
about.a2: The platform charges a 10% service fee on each transaction for both buyer and seller, with a minimum of HK$3 per side. New users enjoy a half-price discount (5%) on their first few transactions, applied automatically at checkout.

sell.title: How to Sell
sell.q1: How do I list a receipt for sale?
sell.a1: Log in and tap '+' on the home screen → Select mall → Enter amount and expiry → List it.
sell.q2: How much can I sell a receipt for?
sell.a2: You set the price yourself. Pricing below face value tends to attract buyers.

buy.title: How to Buy
buy.q1: How do I buy a receipt?
buy.a1: Browse the receipt listings on the home page → Tap the one you want → Confirm interest → Arrange an in-person handover with the seller.
buy.a2: The buyer pays through the platform first (funds held in escrow). Both parties meet in person at the mall to exchange and verify the receipt. Once the buyer confirms 'Received', the system automatically releases payment to the seller.

safety.title: Safety & Protection
safety.a1: BuyTime uses an escrow mechanism: after the buyer pays, funds are held by the platform until the seller delivers and the buyer confirms receipt. If there is a dispute, you can request platform mediation.
safety.q2: What if I have a problem?

disputes.title: Disputes & Refunds
disputes.q1: How long do I have to raise a dispute after the seller marks delivery?
disputes.a1: There is a 15-minute countdown after the seller marks delivery. You must verify the receipt and either confirm receipt (releasing payment) or raise a dispute before it expires. Once the countdown ends, the system auto-confirms and releases payment — refunds will not be accepted after this point.
disputes.q2: What if I confirmed receipt but the parking discount doesn't work?
disputes.a2: Once you confirm receipt, payment is released to the seller and cannot be reversed. Please carefully verify the mall name, spend amount, receipt validity, and parking conditions before confirming. If in doubt, raise a dispute first.
disputes.q3: What if I arrive at the mall and find the receipt is invalid or already used?
disputes.a3: If you are still within the 15-minute countdown, immediately tap 'Raise Dispute' and upload photos of the receipt as evidence. The admin team will handle it within 24 hours. If the countdown has already expired (auto-released), refunds cannot be processed — please verify receipts before confirming.
disputes.q4: What if the seller doesn't show up?
disputes.a4: During the 15-minute countdown, tap 'Raise Dispute' and select 'Seller did not show up'. The admin team will review and issue a refund to the buyer if confirmed. We recommend agreeing on the meeting time and location in the chat beforehand.
disputes.q5: The receipt is real but the parking discount didn't apply at the machine — will I get a refund?
disputes.a5: Receipt validity (including entry time, daily parking rules, etc.) is the responsibility of both parties. The platform is not liable for changes in mall parking policies. We recommend checking parking conditions before purchase and verifying the receipt works on-site before confirming.

s1.title: 1. Platform Nature
s1.body: BuyTime is a Hong Kong mall parking receipt matching platform that helps users who wish to buy or sell mall parking validation receipts find each other. The platform is in Beta testing, operating as an information matching service, not a financial or payment service.

s2.title: 2. Service Fees
s2.body: The platform charges both buyers and sellers a 10% service fee on the transaction amount, with a minimum of HK$3 per side. New users may enjoy a half-price discount (5%) on their first few transactions, applied automatically with no code required. The platform reserves the right to adjust fee rates, and users will be notified in-app in advance of material changes.

s3.title: 3. Transaction Process & Fund Protection
s3.p1: 3.1 The buyer completes payment through the platform, and funds are held in escrow by the platform. The seller will not receive payment until the handover is confirmed.
s3.p2: 3.2 Both parties arrange the in-person receipt exchange and verification at the designated mall. Once the buyer confirms 'Received' (or the system auto-confirms after a timeout), the platform automatically releases payment to the seller.
s3.p3: 3.3 Both parties should verify the following at the time of handover: authenticity and completeness of the receipt; parking validation conditions (mall, amount, expiry). If there is a concern about the receipt, a dispute can be raised through the platform before confirming.

s4.title: 4. Limitation of Liability
s4.body: The platform accepts no legal liability for: the authenticity or validity of receipts; any disputes between buyers and sellers; changes or cancellations to parking validation policies by malls; or any direct or indirect losses arising from transactions. Users understand that transaction risks are borne by both parties; the platform provides matching information only.

s5.title: 5. User Responsibilities
s5.body: Users must ensure that all receipts uploaded are legitimately owned by them. Users must not upload forged, altered, or already-used receipts. Users must provide accurate personal information upon registration. The platform reserves the right to terminate accounts for violations.

s6.title: 6. Personal Data
s6.body: The platform collects and uses user data in accordance with the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, solely for the purpose of platform operations, and will not sell data to third parties.

s7.title: 7. Amendments
s7.body: The platform reserves the right to amend these Terms at any time. Material changes will be notified to users in advance within the App. Continued use of the platform constitutes acceptance of the amended Terms.

s8.title: 8. Governing Law
s8.body: These Terms are governed by the laws of Hong Kong. Any disputes shall be submitted to Hong Kong courts.
